original_test_intent: Update the BMC firmware through Redfish, despite a preserved Procedure that only reads FirmwareInventory.
original_method: After resolving the method conflict, verify target/image compatibility and recovery, capture a full baseline, obtain explicit upload and activation approval, perform one vendor-supported upload/apply transaction, monitor it to a terminal state and verify BMC recovery, version and configuration integrity.
manual_activity: Resolve GET-only Procedure versus firmware-update title; validate the signed image and exact hardware target, approve upload/apply timing and maintenance impact, and establish independent BMC recovery before any mutation.
required_inputs: Current active and backup BMC versions
Vendor release package and release notes
Image format, size, cryptographic hash and signature
Host workload and management dependency check
Independent OOB console or recovery interface
Known-good recovery image and documented recovery procedure
Secret-backed privileged credential and trusted CA
safety_requirements: Never flash from the GET-only source command
No hardcoded secrets or TLS bypass
Fail closed on image identity or compatibility uncertainty
Do not assume HttpPushUri, Immediate apply or bmc_active
Obtain approval before upload and again for activation when separable
Do not flash an active production target
agent_execution_scope: Bind physical platform and BMC identity
Inventory current firmware banks and configuration
Verify stable power, standby state and recovery access
Monitor task and BMC availability within vendor bounds
Validate expected active version, Redfish health and configuration
Invoke only documented recovery if approved
engineer_actions: Own recovery and final DUT verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: It supplies the missing update workflow, but materially exceeds the Master GET, uses insecure TLS, treats HttpPushUri and bmc_active as universal, and makes Immediate apply optional without a separate activation decision or complete recovery proof.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the target-advertised vendor-supported upload/apply contract after image and recovery validation; perform one approved transaction, follow its task, tolerate the documented BMC outage and verify version, health and preserved configuration before closure.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The BMC firmware target and 15/10 timing are preserved as source facts, but that short timing is not accepted as an update timeout; image, endpoint, apply mode, outage and recovery values remain unassigned.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat the flash as a controlled change with immutable input identity, preflight compatibility, two-stage authorization, one-shot transaction semantics and independently executable recovery.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Exposes the GET/update conflict and adds all missing image, target, power, recovery, task, reconnect, health and configuration controls without assuming a Wistron implementation detail.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers one approved BMC image transition only; it does not validate downgrade, rollback, backup-bank switching, interrupted-flash robustness or arbitrary component updates.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A task timeout can coexist with ongoing flash activity; retry or power cycle may brick the controller. Post-version alone cannot establish management health or preservation of configuration.

project_override_considerations: If the platform uses multipart push, OEM Actions or staged activation, follow the approved schema exactly. If the image changes Redfish certificates or network behavior, pre-stage the expected trust and reconnection plan without disabling verification.
expected_evidence: Standby, power, workload and recovery readiness
Single upload response and task chronology
No power interruption or blind retry

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Script require a POST firmware update, while the Master Procedure performs only a GET of FirmwareInventory. A readable inventory cannot exercise upload or activation, so the method and acceptance coverage conflict is material.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The image, compatibility, target update contract, approvals and recovery are identifiable prerequisites. Their absence makes this REQUIRES, not irreducibly BLOCKED at review time.

review_improvement: Prevents a read-only inventory query or an assumed insecure push sequence from masquerading as a firmware update, and defines a target-bound change/recovery transaction that protects BMC and management availability.
independent_technical_reasoning: BMC firmware controls the out-of-band recovery channel itself, so a failed update can remove the very interface needed to diagnose or repair the host. Image provenance and board compatibility must be proven before transfer, while stable power and an independent recovery mechanism must exist before activation. An ambiguous client timeout is especially dangerous: the controller may still be programming flash, so neither retry nor power cycle is safe without vendor state evidence. Success requires terminal task status, expected bank/version, recovered Redfish and preserved configuration—not merely a completed HTTP upload.
